Great code is only half the job

Cadpeople is hiring a frontend developer in Aarhus who writes solid code, understands the client, designs the system, and makes it feel right.

For 30 years, we've made the complex simple for companies like Vestas, Ørsted, Grundfos, Novo Nordisk and Fred. Olsen. We do it with 3D, XR, digital training simulators, virtual campuses, and digital learning, all built on our in-house frameworks.

The craft is changing too. AI tools already have a big impact on how we develop, and we're on a journey to strengthen our AI coding capabilities. But AI only pays off in the hands of developers with real knowledge and experience. That's why we look for systems thinking, client dialogue, and close collaboration with our creatives, as much as we do code.

What you'll do

You'll build bespoke applications for large enterprise clients, from the first workshop to the live solution. Typical work:

• Turn client needs into systems. Join client meetings and workshops, ask the right questions, and shape the solution before anyone writes code.

• Think across frameworks. Combine our in-house building blocks (Vue.js and Three.js frontends, Digital simulators, Umbraco headless CMS, .NET microservices on Azure, and Electron for offline use) into the right architecture for each case.

• Use what we've already built. Draw on experience from delivered projects to show the client what's possible, and to avoid building the same thing twice.

• Help shape how we build with AI. Use AI tools in your daily work, and help us strengthen our AI coding capabilities as we go.

• Work closely with creatives. Art directors, 3D artists, learning specialists, and project managers are your daily team. You make their ideas run in the browser, on a kiosk, or in a headset.

• Strengthen the foundation. Improve the frameworks on which every future project stands.

Who you are

We don't expect you to know it all. But you'll recognise yourself in most of this:

• You have at least 3 years of experience as a frontend developer, with solid JavaScript/TypeScript and Vue.js skills.

• You think in systems, not just screens: APIs, data, hosting, security and how it all fits together.

• You use AI coding tools fluently, and you still understand, review, and own every line that ships.

• You can explain technical choices to a client who isn't technical, in English. Danish is a plus.

• You care about how things look and feel, and you enjoy working with designers and 3D artists.

• You think big. A request for "an e-learning module" makes you wonder whether it should be a simulator, a virtual campus, or an AI coach.

• It's a plus if you know Three.js, WebGL, Umbraco, Node.js, .NET, Azure, CI/CD and security by design (OWASP Top 10).

Your education matters less than your curiosity and how well you work with others.

What you get

• Work that matters. Train wind turbine technicians, onboard energy workers, and help industrial companies explain products that change the world, often with a sustainability angle.

• Big clients, small team. Enterprise-scale projects with the speed and closeness of a 50-person agency in Aarhus and Edinburgh.

• A global parent with reach. Cadpeople is part of RelyOn, a global safety and training provider with more than 50 facilities worldwide. That gives us stability, new clients, and the chance to see your work train people in safety-critical jobs around the world.

• A head start on every project. Our own tested frameworks mean you start from a solid foundation, not a blank page.

• A say in what comes next. We're building up our AI coding capabilities, and this role can help shape how we get there.

• A creative workplace. An office in the heart of Aarhus, surrounded by people who make 3D, film, XR and learning. See our culture.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short application. A classic application is welcome, as long as it sounds like you. Generic AI-written applications will not be prioritised.

Want to stand out? You can add something small that shows your character and how you'd fit in at Cadpeople. It's optional, and it doesn't need to be big or complex. For example:

• A story about a time you turned a vague client need into something that worked.

• A short video, even filmed on your phone, about something you built or care about.

• A skill or tool, like a small AI agent, workflow or utility you made to work smarter.

• A thought on one of our cases: what you'd have done differently, or how you'd take it further.

Our office language is Danish, and we use English with many of our clients. You don't need to be fluent in Danish, but it helps if you understand it.

Questions about the role? Contact Nikolaj Have, CTO, at nikolaj.have@cadpeople.dk.

Start as soon as possible, or by agreement. All applications are treated confidentially, and submitted material is deleted after 6 months in line with GDPR.

**About The Company

**Founded in 2019, Novutech is a dynamic digital transformation partner with a team of over 60 consultants across Europe. We specialize in finance-focused digital transformation projects for international scale-ups and mid-sized enterprises. Our expertise lies in leveraging a core tech stack and the experience from hundreds of successful projects. We are committed to designing, delivering, and supporting end-to-end solutions that drive growth and efficiency.

**About The Role

**As a Senior Business Consultant, you will play a key role in delivering impactful digital transformation projects for our clients. Leveraging your NetSuite expertise, you will lead complex implementations, oversee advanced configurations, and act as a trusted advisor. You will also mentor junior consultants and progressively develop your people management skills, with the opportunity to lead your own team in the future.

• Lead and execute end-to-end NetSuite implementation projects, from requirements gathering to go-live and post-implementation support.

• Oversee advanced NetSuite configurations and customizations to meet customer needs, acting as a Subject Matter Expert.

• Configure, customize, and optimize NetSuite modules according to client needs.

• Monitor, test, validate, and resolve advanced problems in NetSuite areas.

• Maintain and document high-level processes and complex customizations for external stakeholders.

• Act as a trusted advisor to clients, providing best practices and recommendations.

• Support change management and user adoption initiatives.

• Manage overall relationships as Customer Success Manager for medium to large customers, handling tickets, organizing calls, and ensuring quality.

• Contribute to project planning, scoping, and estimation activities, collaborating with internal teams and stakeholders to ensure project success.

• Participate in sales and presales activities as an expert.

• Mentor and supervise business and tech analysts, providing guidance, feedback, and supporting their development through activities such as regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and career growth planning, while ensuring high standards in methodology and consulting practices.

• Act as the right hand of the Manager or Director, upholding company values and amplifying leadership messages.

• Contribute to internal projects fostering innovation and growth through entrepreneurial ideas and OKRs.

• Stay updated on NetSuite developments and actively share knowledge with the team.

Why joining Novutech?

• Be part of a fast-growing company with a startup spirit, and enjoy a friendly environment with tremendous colleagues and a hybrid work setup.

• Experience a place where you can grow, learn, and make a significant impact.

• Benefit from a good work-life balance, fostering both personal and professional well-being.

• Enjoy international exposure by collaborating closely with colleagues across our global offices, enriching your professional experience and broadening your cultural understanding.

• Minimum 3-5 years of experience in NetSuite consulting, implementation, or administration.

• Proven track record of successful NetSuite implementations and advanced configuration.

• Strong understanding of business processes (Finance, Accounting, Operations, etc.).

• Experience working in a consulting environment or with multiple clients.

• Demonstrated experience in mentoring, coaching, or supervising junior team members.

• Customer Success Management experience is a plus.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to build strong client relationships.

• Analytical and problem-solving mindset, with attention to detail.

• Ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative, international team.

• Entrepreneurial spirit and drive for continuous improvement.

• Fluent in English; knowledge of French or Dutch is a plus.

• Willingness to travel occasionally within Europe as required.

If you are excited about the opportunity to make a difference and grow with us, we want to hear from you! Join Novutech and be part of an adventure that’s shaping the future of digital transformation.

Sr Business Operations Manager

Department: GMA Business Operations

Location: Søborg, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Sr Business Operations Manager, you will help Global Medical Affairs (GMA) leadership make clearer, faster decisions on strategy, budget and priorities. You will advise senior leaders, lead complex projects where the problem is not yet defined, and co-own a key process that GMA teams rely on. Your work turns ambiguity into decisions, so medical affairs colleagues can focus their time and resources where they matter most for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

• Master’s degree in business, finance, sciences, engineering or a similar field.

• 5–7 years of relevant experience leading complex, cross-functional strategic projects and owning process improvement in a complex organisation.

• Experience leading financial planning and budget processes, challenging financial assumptions and aligning Finance and senior stakeholders around priorities and decisions.

• A proven ability to frame ambiguous problems, influence senior leaders, guide contributors and turn analysis into decisions.

• Excellent executive communication, strategic judgement and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence without authority and sustain alignment across senior stakeholder groups.

• Cultural awareness and adaptability, and a collaborative way of coaching colleagues.

What you’ll do

Your role combines three connected workstreams: partnering with GMA leaders, owning the budget process and leading projects. Together, they help GMA work with more clarity and speed.

• Advise the head of your assigned GMA area on the annual strategy process and its translation into budget priorities, framing trade-offs and challenging assumptions, dependencies and options.

• Co-own the budget process area with a team colleague, setting direction for templates, guidance and best practice, and leading adoption across GMA.

• Lead highly complex and ambiguous strategic projects: frame the problem, define scope and governance, set milestones and risk responses, and deliver on time, within budget and to the required quality.

• Strengthen governance by clarifying decisions, accountability and follow-up across interdependent work.

• Turn evidence into concise, data-driven recommendations, and prepare analyses, memos and presentations that shape GMA Leadership Team decisions.

• Share what you learn, improve common team methods and mentor colleagues, so the team stays resilient and consistent.

Who you’ll work with

You will join GMA Business Operations in Product & Portfolio Strategy, where colleagues connect commercial strategy, medical affairs and business development across therapy areas to help guide the Novo portfolio and strengthen competitiveness. You will report to the Director, GMA Business Operations, and work closely with your team colleagues to ensure success across the unit.

Your day-to-day partners include the GMA Leadership Team, leaders and specialists across GMA and medical affairs worldwide, Finance partner, and colleagues in Strategy, Executive Office and PMO functions. You will also have occasional contact with external parties.

The role is global in scope, with stakeholders across the world and minimal travel expected. Your influence comes from building trust, creating clarity and aligning functions whose priorities may differ.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to define your own approach to complex, unclear assignments, with minimal guidance and room to make your voice heard at senior level. You will grow by working across GMA and supporting functions, learning from colleagues and sharing your expertise through mentoring and strategic sparring.

We expect high standards and honest, direct conversations, and we support you to perform at your best.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

**JOB SUMMARY

**We are looking for an FP&A Specialist to strengthen our Corporate FP&A team and take ownership of cash flow forecasting, balance sheet planning, working capital management, and other key planning activities below Adjusted EBITDA across the Group.

Reporting directly to the Head of FP&A, you will play a key role in advancing our financial planning capabilities and driving transparency across cash flow, liquidity, and balance sheet performance. You will work closely with Accounting, Tax, Controlling, regional Finance teams, and key business stakeholders to ensure robust planning processes and high-quality management reporting.

This is a unique opportunity to:

• Take ownership of the Group's cash flow, balance sheet, and working capital planning agenda, helping to improve cash generation and support management decision-making.

• Shape and develop our Workday Adaptive Planning capabilities, leading key initiatives to establish scalable planning models and reporting structures.

• Work across markets and functions, partnering with regional Finance teams and senior stakeholders to strengthen forecasting, reporting, and business insight throughout the organization.

The successful candidate will help establish best-in-class planning processes that connect P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow forecasting, providing management with greater visibility into liquidity, working capital performance, and long-term value creation. The role is a full-time role and reports to the Head of Group Financial Planning & Analysis.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Own the Group's cash flow planning across forecast, budget, and long-range planning cycles.

• Drive the development of balance sheet forecasting capabilities and ensure alignment between P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow planning.

• Lead the implementation and continuous development of cash flow and balance sheet planning models in Workday Adaptive Planning.

• Define business requirements and partner closely with the BI Team to improve planning processes, reporting capabilities, and system functionality.

• Partner with Accounting, Controlling, Tax, and regional Finance teams to strengthen cash flow and balance sheet reporting, improve forecast accuracy, and establish clear ownership across planning activities.

• Develop and maintain monthly cash flow, balance sheet, and working capital reporting, including variance analysis, key risks and opportunities, and actionable management insights.

• Establish and maintain a clear RACI framework across Finance for balance sheet and cash flow planning, forecasting, and follow-up activities.

• Develop driver-based forecasting methodologies for key working capital metrics, including inventory, receivables, payables, and other material balance sheet accounts.

• Monitor working capital performance and identify opportunities to improve cash conversion and optimize working capital.

• Partner with Operations, Supply Chain, Accounting, and Controlling to strengthen understanding of working capital drivers and improve forecast accuracy.

• Support Executive Management and Board reporting by providing insights on cash generation, liquidity, working capital performance, and financial risks and opportunities.

• Drive continuous improvement of forecasting methodologies, planning processes, and financial transparency across the organization.

• Support the ongoing development of FP&A capabilities by integrating balance sheet and cash flow considerations into strategic and long-range planning processes.

**WHO YOU ARE

**You are a curious and analytical finance professional with a passion for turning data into insights and helping the business make better decisions. You enjoy working across functions, building strong stakeholder relationships, and taking ownership of complex planning processes.

You thrive in a dynamic and growing environment and are comfortable navigating between operational details and the bigger picture. You enjoy driving improvements, challenging assumptions, and creating structure where it is needed.

You are comfortable working across Finance functions and partnering with regional Finance teams to improve forecasting, strengthen financial transparency, and drive continuous improvement. Most importantly, you are proactive, structured, and motivated by creating impact through high-quality financial planning and analysis.

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING

**

• 5+ years of experience within FP&A, Financial Controlling, Corporate Finance, or a similar role.

• Strong understanding of financial statements, budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning.

• Experience working with cash flow forecasting, working capital, balance sheet analysis, or investment planning.

• Solid financial modelling and analytical skills, including advanced Excel capabilities.

• Experience with Workday Adaptive Planning or other EPM/planning tools is an advantage.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• A proactive mindset and a passion for improving processes, systems, and ways of working.

• Experience from retail, hospitality, food & beverage, consumer goods, or other multi-site businesses is considered a plus.

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars - there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

**Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

****ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!

As ESG Reporting Advisor, you will help prepare Novo’s ESG reporting, including the Sustainability statement in the Annual Report, and make sure the data behind it is accurate, transparent and trusted. Investors, regulators, employees and other external stakeholders rely on this reporting to understand Novo’s sustainability commitments and progress. You will be responsible for selected metrics, EU Taxonomy reporting and to improve our data collection and controlling processes.

What you’ll bring

The ESG space is changing fast. You will do well here if you:

• Thrive in a high-pace environment where things are anything but at steady state.

• Enjoy working in a large organisation with many stakeholders and handling many different tasks at once.

• Bring a pragmatic, can-do attitude.

• Communicate clearly and interact confidently with stakeholders at all levels.

Useful, but not essential: one or several of the following

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree related to ESG topics, business or auditing.

• Minimum 3+ years’ experience in sustainability, ESG reporting or as an ESG consultant.

• Knowledge of ESG reporting methodologies and frameworks, such as CSRD, EU Taxonomy and the GHG Protocol.

• Experience with ESG assurance and internal controls.

What you’ll do

You will help deliver high-quality ESG reporting and strengthen how it is produced. Your work will include:

• Preparing Novo’s ESG reporting, including the Sustainability statement in the Annual Report.

• Taking responsibility for selected metrics (climate, pollution, nature, circularity, own workforce, business conduct or equitable access) and making sure they are reported accurately and transparently.

• Working closely with stakeholders across the business on data collection and carrying out controls and checks on key ESG metrics.

• Owning our EU Taxonomy reporting.

• Improving data collection and consolidation processes and strengthening the internal ESG control environment.

• Driving continuous improvement of existing processes with AI and other digital tools.

Who you’ll work with

You will be part of ESG Reporting at our headquarters in Bagsværd, outside Copenhagen. The ESG Reporting team has 8 colleagues across Denmark and India. ESG Reporting sits within Finance under the CFO, as part of Corporate Accounting, led by Rikke Ryttergaard Andersen. Corporate Accounting has approximately 40 colleagues with a great mix of age, gender and nationality.

What you can expect here

You will work on a topic that is moving quickly, with room to contribute your expertise and shape how ESG reporting is done. You will build new skills by working across the business and by using AI and digital tools in your daily work. You will be supported to perform at your best, trusted to take ownership and encouraged to speak up when things are stalling.

HR Specialist.

The candidate:

Systematic, structured and business-oriented – focus on execution and outcome

You can balance the “thinker and doer” – in other words, you like to create structures and processes, most often based on IT tools and to execute and create results in the business. You manage to convert the strategic vision for HR into concrete efforts with structure and action which create results and work in practice.

Furthermore, you are a role model for the values, the good colleague and collaboration across the organization. You are a team player and ensure everyone, as a team, reach our goals.

You are based on the site in Aarhus with a few travel days per year. You speak and write Danish and English on a professional level. In addition, you are a seasoned SAP and Microsoft Office user. It’s an exciting time to join Tactile. We're a diverse team of storytellers, puzzle enthusiasts, and casual mobile game creators. Our story began in 2008 in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, and since then, we have experienced continuous growth, establishing ourselves as one of the largest gaming companies in Denmark. In more recent years, we have been scaling fast, in large part thanks to the success of a little game called Lily’s Garden. Now we’re on a mission to solidify our position as one of the leaders in creating out-of-the-ordinary casual puzzle games.

With more than 350 talented individuals, we are a mix of over 50 nationalities and 43% women. We truly appreciate the richness of different experiences and perspectives that Tactilers bring to the game. This is why we foster a lean organisational culture, in which each individual is encouraged to take responsibility, be open, and grow in their own way. We pride ourselves on cultivating a studio environment that avoids crunch, fosters your skills regardless of your discipline, and provides a space for you to be creative alongside other passionate and invested storytellers.

🚀 Your role & impact:

We're currently growing our Core team and are on the lookout for another Product Designer to join our team of talented engineers.

The Core team builds the internal tools behind Tactile own LiveOps, Marketing and Data operations, the backbone of our studio. We're looking for a second Product Designer to join Joy and our engineers in designing business-critical tools that every team at Tactile depends on.

This role is based in our Copenhagen office.

How we design:

• Our tools are data-heavy: dashboards, large tables, complex filters, multi-step workflows. Static mockups can't show how they behave with real data, so we prototype first, in code. We use Claude Code and agentic workflows to build working prototypes, and those prototypes are what we hand off to developers. Figma is still where we sketch and brainstorm

• AI amplifies our design. It doesn't do design for us. It lets us take on complex workflows that used to get skipped because they took too much effort

jobs.description:
The position is based in Roskilde or Warsaw at BEC Financial Technologies' headquarters. The position is organizationally anchored in Service Integration & Security with reference to the Head of Projects & Continuity.

The Service Integration & Security area is responsible for strengthening BEC’s operational resilience and ensuring that critical business services can continue through disruption. We work closely with business areas, banking specialists, risk and compliance functions, and technology stakeholders to establish a shared understanding of business criticality, dependencies, continuity requirements, and recovery priorities.

As Business Continuity Manager, you will lead and develop BEC’s Business Impact Analysis and business criticality processes. You will engage with business owners across BEC to identify critical services and processes, assess the consequences of disruption, clarify dependencies, and define proportionate continuity and recovery requirements. The role requires strong business understanding, facilitation skills, and the ability to translate banking needs and regulatory expectations into clear priorities and practical actions.

At BEC, we prefer to collaborate often in the office, while also offering the opportunity to work remotely on average up to 1 day per week.

Primary tasks and responsibilities include:

Continuity & resilience framework:

• Developing and maintaining BEC’s business continuity management framework with a clear business and customer perspective

• Owning the governance and methodology for Business Impact Analysis and business criticality assessments

• Ensuring that continuity priorities and requirements reflect customer impact, banking obligations, financial exposure, regulatory expectations, and operational dependencies

• Supporting the development and maintenance of business continuity plans and ensuring alignment with relevant standards and regulation

Business Impact Analysis (BIA) ownership & execution:

• Planning, facilitating, and driving Business Impact Analyses across BEC’s business areas and shared functions

• Helping business owners identify critical customer services, products, processes, and activities, including the impact of disruption over time

• Facilitating consistent criticality assessments and supporting management decisions on priorities, tolerances, and continuity requirements

• Identifying and documenting key dependencies on people, suppliers, facilities, information, applications, and other business services

• Consolidating results into management insight for BEC’s most critical services, business impacts, dependencies, and resilience priorities

Coordination & stakeholder engagement:

• Building strong relationships with business owners, banking specialists, risk and compliance functions, service owners, and senior stakeholders

• Leading workshops and interviews that turn business knowledge into clear, evidence-based impact and criticality assessments

• Challenging assumptions constructively and creating alignment where business priorities, regulatory requirements, and operational capabilities differ

• Translating business continuity needs into clear requirements for relevant operational and technology stakeholders without being the technical solution owner

Validation****, exercises & continuous improvement:

• Validating BIA and criticality outcomes through business reviews, continuity exercises, incidents, and organizational changes

Governance, reporting & insight:

• Preparing clear management reporting on business criticality, BIA coverage, key risks, dependencies, gaps, and improvement priorities

• High visibility across the organization and interaction with senior stakeholders

• The opportunity to shape and evolve BEC’s continuity and BIA practices

• A collaborative environment with strong professional expertise

• A role with tangible impact on BEC’s ability to operate under disruption

R30528 Senior Group Financial Controller with consolidation focus, GN

Do you want to make your financial knowledge count? Imagine a possibility where you will be responsible for financial excellence by supporting and further developing the finance function in a global organization.

The team you will be part of

As a Senior Group Financial Controller at GN, you will join Group Finance and take a central role in ensuring accurate, timely and high-quality consolidated financial reporting.

Working closely with local finance teams, Group controllers and external auditors, you will drive the consolidation process while helping to simplify, standardise and strengthen the Group’s closing and reporting set-up.

Your contribution is appreciated and your responsibilities will include:

Consolidation, closing and Group reporting

You will own and drive the monthly, quarterly and annual Group consolidation process, ensuring a robust, efficient and well-documented close.

You will:

• Lead and coordinate the Group consolidation process, from entity reporting to consolidated reporting

• Review reporting from Group entities and perform consolidation entries, including intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation and other Group adjustments.

• Support the preparation of the consolidated financial statements

• Act as a on of the key point of contact for subsidiaries during the closing process, providing guidance on reporting and consolidation matters

• Support the transition of selected consolidation and reporting activities from external providers to an in-house Group Finance set-up

Process optimisation and reporting development

A key part of the role is to make the closing and reporting process faster, simpler and more reliable.

You will:

• Identify and drive improvements to closing, consolidation and reporting processes, including automation and standardisation opportunities

• Develop and maintain reporting packages in the consolidation system and process documentation

• Support the development and maintenance of consolidation and reporting systems and act as a key user where relevant

Financial controlling and collaboration

In close collaboration with other Group controllers, you will support the review and quality assurance of financial reporting from subsidiaries.

You will:

• Review and challenge selected financial information reported by subsidiaries

• Follow up on reporting issues, unusual developments and data-quality matters

• Contribute to the continued development of controls, governance and documentation within the Group reporting process

To perform well in the role, we imagine that you:

You are structured, proactive and analytical, with a strong sense of ownership and quality. You enjoy working with fixed deadlines, multiple stakeholders and continuous process improvement.

Moreover, you have a keen sense of quality, and you:

• Hold a master’s degree in finance, accounting, auditing, or a similar field

• Have several years of relevant experience from Group consolidation, financial reporting, or an international audit firm

• Have hands-on experience with consolidation processes and a good understanding of the flow from local entity reporting to Group reporting

• Have experience with financial reporting systems. Experience with systems such as OneStream, HFM or Microsoft Dynamics is an advantage

• Are comfortable working independently, driving tasks to completion and collaborating across functions and geographies

• Speak and write fluent English

We encourage you to apply

Even if you don’t match all the above-mentioned skills, we welcome your application if you think you have transferrable skills. We highly value a mindset and motivation that align with our core values, to not only ensure growth for you, but for your team and the wider GN organization as well.

We are focused on an inclusive recruitment process

All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. As such, we encourage you to submit your CV without a photo to ensure an equal and fair application process.

Should you have any special requirements for the interview, please let the Hiring Manager know upon accepting invitation to interview.
